headline: Louisiana health officials warn against amoeba infections from tap water
summary: The Louisiana Department of Health has issued a warning against using tap water for nasal rinses or contact lens cleaning after two serious Acanthamoeba infections were reported this year, including one fatal case. While tap water has not been confirmed as the source, health officials urge the public to use distilled or previously boiled water for nasal irrigation and contact lens care to prevent rare but potentially devastating infections.

headline: Huge bipartisan majorities of Ohioans want a fix to Social Security, new poll shows
summary: A poll by the Peter G. Peterson Foundation found that 85% of likely Ohio voters deem it important to fix Social Security due to pending insolvency, with 75% more likely to vote for a Senate candidate with a plan to prevent automatic benefit cuts.

headline: Secretary of education says Virginia will ‘move the achievement needle forward’
summary: Virginia's governor focuses on early education and college readiness in K-12 education; priorities include improving instructional quality, strengthening educator workforce, expanding childcare access.

headline: Shakopee man from Nicaragua deported to Central African Republic
summary: In its effort to deport millions of immigrants, the Trump administration has been sending individuals with deportation protections to authoritarian countries, like the Central African Republic, in exchange for cash or concessions. Despite having a court order barring his deportation and a pending habeas corpus petition, Kenis Lopez Gonzalez, a Minnesotan with no criminal record, was tricked into boarding a plane and deported to the Central African Republic, where he remains in detention. His lawyers are challenging his deportation, with a hearing scheduled on Dec. 29. This case raises questions about the legality and human rights implications of third-country deportations.

headline: Hayes takes over Finance as Ferguson announces early changes to leadership
summary: Senate Finance Committee to be led by Sen. Antonio Hayes (D-Baltimore City), first Black lawmaker to hold the position. Sen. Cory McCray (D-Baltimore City) appointed as vice chair of Senate Budget and Taxation Committee, facing $3 billion structural budget gap. No specific budget cuts or increases mentioned, but potential tax increases discussed, including sales tax changes.

headline: Howard lawmakers’ bill would set higher tax rates on propose ICE facility in Elkridge
summary: Maryland lawmakers introduced a bill allowing Howard County to levy higher property taxes on a proposed ICE detention facility in Elkridge, aiming to offset fiscal impacts on the county. The bill comes after a federal court rejected county emergency legislation attempting to block the facility. Community leaders support the bill, while ICE states it won't halt deportations due to any tax.

headline: For the record: Fresno man deported by ICE had previous illegal crossings
summary: ICE waited until after a CalMatters story published to reveal that a profiled immigrant, Luis Arreguin, had been deported five times, raising questions about ICE's transparency and communication with media.

headline: Did Trump invest more money in rural California health ahead of the election?
summary: The Trump administration announced a $233.6 million investment in California rural health, but it's California's share of a $50 billion national fund approved in 2025, not new money. This investment aims to improve healthcare in rural areas, including the Central Valley, where Republican incumbents face tough questions about federal healthcare cuts. Despite the investment, California stands to lose $30 billion annually for its Medi-Cal program due to Medicaid cuts in the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, potentially doubling the state's uninsured rate.

headline: Un juez rechaza la solicitud del gobierno de Trump para anular 20,000 votos electorales de California
summary: A federal judge in California rejected the Trump administration's request to remove 20,000 ballots due to voter citizenship concerns, citing potential chaos and disruption to the electoral process, and protecting voting rights of generations of Americans.

headline: Dolores Huerta “se mantuvo en la lucha” durante siete décadas, inspirando a generaciones de californianos
summary: "Dolores Huerta, a key figure in California's farmworker movement, passed away at 96. Despite recent controversies surrounding César Chávez, activists pushed for Huerta's legacy to replace his. Huerta's lifelong advocacy for farmworkers' rights continues to inspire activism."

headline: Trump and Freedom Caucus approval, election confidence: Three takeaways from a Wyoming survey ahead of the general election
summary: In Wyoming's 2026 election survey, a majority disapprove of Trump's job handling (49%), with only 39% approving. Most Wyomingites (51%) disapprove of the Wyoming Freedom Caucus, while 56% have confidence in state election reliability. These polling insights indicate potential political shifts in Wyoming.

headline: During wave of closures, Morrisey says school funding issue will ‘dominate’ 2027 legislative session
summary: West Virginia faces potential school closures due to funding issues; Gov. Morrisey prioritizes addressing school funding in next session; State school board proposes restructuring funding formula, with special education reforms costing $190 million; Morrisey cautions against increased spending without efficient use of funds.

headline: Mountain State Poll shows close races for federal offices
summary: The 39th Mountain State Poll by MSU-B shows competitive races for Montana's U.S. Senate and western U.S. House seats, with Kurt Alme (R) leading Seth Bodnar (I) by 4 points and Sam Forstag (D) leading Aaron Flint (R) by 17 points. The poll, with a 3.6% margin of error, also reveals high disapproval for Congress and Montana's federal delegation. Governor Gianforte has the highest approval rating at 35%.

headline: Weddle request to move his case to Franklin County is denied
summary: Former London Mayor Randall Weddle faces felony charges for allegedly circumventing campaign finance limits to benefit Gov. Andy Beshear's reelection. A judge denied Weddle's motion to move the trial, stating the actions significantly impacted Laurel County. The case could influence political donations transparency and accountability.

headline: Bird flu detected in Iowa commercial flock for first time nearly a year
summary: Bird flu, HPAI H5N1, detected in Iowa's Sac County commercial turkey flock of 44,400 birds; governor issues disaster proclamation to aid containment; first commercial flock outbreak since Dec 2025; public health risk low, no known person-to-person spread.

headline: Western Alaska voters asked to weigh familiar state House candidates with similar stances
summary: In the Alaska House District 38 race, incumbent Nellie Jimmie (D) and challenger CJ McCormick (D) have similar views, but McCormick opposes the Donlin Gold mine while Jimmie initially was neutral, now opposes it. Republican Willy Keppel also opposes the mine. Polls show McCormick and Jimmie neck-and-neck, with Keppel close behind.
